title: A Plan Says Whether Its Run Completes Its Source Spec

ground.note: Run completion: completes the plan, then rides the source spec along whenever the chain gate lets it, and reports a blocked spec as a skip.

findDependentPlans and the chain gate: a spec cannot go terminal while a live plan under docs/plans/ (archive/ skipped) names it. checkPlanRunnable applies the same plan frontmatter decoder to loose plans.

context:
A plan names the spec it implements in its frontmatter:

    ---
    status: Approved
    source-spec: docs/specs/2609291000-widgets.md
    approved:
      date: 2026-10-01
      baseline: 1a2b3c4
    ---

Spec 27 put artifact completion on the run branch. When a run's final phase is green, phax completes the plan there. It then completes the plan's source spec too, unless the chain gate refuses: the gate keeps a spec live while another live plan under docs/plans/ names it, and reports the skip with the blocking plans. The merge then lands the work and the record in one gesture.

The approval fingerprint covers the plan's whole frontmatter except `status` and `approved`. A headless plan has a JSON sidecar, the plan document, which mirrors `sourceSpec`. phax forces that mirror to the `--spec` value of `phax artifact new plan`. `phax-plan.json`, the extracted plan, holds the run and its phases and no lineage.
problem:
The chain gate is the only thing that stops a run from completing a spec, and it sees only plans that already exist. Some specs ship in several plans authored one at a time, each after the previous one lands; schemas-package's five plans were written this way. When such a run ends, no other live plan exists yet, so the first plan's run completes the spec. It moves the spec to archive/ and deletes its approval record while plans 2–5 are still to come.

This happened on schemas-package plan 1/5 (PR #104, 2026-09-29) and again on plans 2 and 3. Each time the completion commit had to be reverted by hand on the PR branch. Nothing persisted says how many plans a spec will have, so phax cannot tell the last plan from the first. Only the plan's author knows, and the plan has no way to say it.

productGoal.statement: Every plan with a source spec states whether its run completes that spec. A run completes the spec only when its plan says so, and the chain gate still applies on top. A plan that does not complete its spec leaves it untouched, and the run's output and its review handoff (so its PR body) say so. The last plan of a multi-plan spec keeps spec 27's guarantee: the spec's completion lands in the same merge as that plan's work.
productGoal.guidingRule: A run completes a spec only when its plan says it is the last; phax never infers it.

terminology.definition: The plan frontmatter key that says whether the plan's run completes its source spec. `true` or `false`. It is present exactly when `source-spec` names a spec.
A plan with `completes-spec: true`: the last plan of its spec, by its author's statement.
A plan with `completes-spec: false`: more plans of the same spec are to come.
Spec 22 §5.4, unchanged: a spec may go terminal only while no live plan declaring it as source is non-terminal.
A plan file directly under docs/plans/, not under docs/plans/archive/.
What run completion did to the source spec. One of three: completed; kept because live plans block it; kept because the plan does not complete it.

requirements.title: The plan states whether it completes its spec
requirements.statement: The system shall decide whether a plan's run completes its source spec only from the plan's `completes-spec` frontmatter key, a boolean carried beside `source-spec` by every plan whose `source-spec` names a spec.

requirements.title: A plan with a source spec must say it
requirements.statement: IF a plan whose `source-spec` names a spec has no `completes-spec` key, or a value other than `true` or `false`, THEN artifact validation SHALL refuse the plan with exit code 12, naming `completes-spec`, in every command that validates a plan, including `phax plans lint`.

requirements.title: A spec-less plan carries no completes-spec
requirements.statement: IF a plan whose `source-spec` is `null` carries a `completes-spec` key THEN artifact validation SHALL refuse the plan with exit code 12, naming `completes-spec` as inconsistent with `source-spec: null`.

requirements.title: A completing plan rides its spec along
requirements.statement: WHEN a run completes a plan whose `completes-spec` is `true` THE system SHALL attempt the source spec's completion exactly as today: it completes the spec on the run branch when the chain gate is clear, and reports the skip naming the blocking plans when it is not.

requirements.title: A non-completing plan never touches its spec
requirements.statement: WHEN a run completes a plan whose `completes-spec` is `false` THE system SHALL leave the source spec's status, location and approval record file unchanged and make no spec commit on the run branch.

requirements.title: Run output names the non-completing plan
requirements.statement: WHEN a run completes a plan whose `completes-spec` is `false` THE system SHALL report in its run completion output that the source spec was kept because the plan does not complete it.

requirements.title: The review handoff states the spec outcome
requirements.statement: WHERE the completed plan declares a source spec THE system SHALL state the spec outcome (completed, kept because live plans block it, or kept because the plan does not complete it) in the run's review handoff, and therefore in the PR body built from it.

requirements.title: The value is part of what was approved
requirements.statement: WHEN the `completes-spec` value of an Approved plan changes after its approval THE system SHALL report the plan as `self-changed`.

requirements.title: Plan creation sets the value
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact new plan` is invoked with `--spec` and exactly one of `--last` or `--not-last` THE system SHALL write `completes-spec: true` or `completes-spec: false` respectively into the new plan's frontmatter, after `source-spec`.

requirements.title: Plan creation refuses an unstated or meaningless value
requirements.statement: IF `phax artifact new plan` is given `--spec` with neither or both of `--last` and `--not-last`, or either flag without `--spec`, THEN the system SHALL refuse with exit code 12 before writing anything.

requirements.title: Headless authoring mirrors the CLI value
requirements.statement: WHERE `phax artifact new plan` runs with `--headless` THE system SHALL set the plan document's `completesSpec` to the value the flags gave (`null` without `--spec`), whatever the session returned, and render the same value into the plan's frontmatter.

requirements.title: The plan document carries completesSpec per variant
requirements.statement: IF a plan document lacks `completesSpec`, or carries a boolean `completesSpec` beside `sourceSpec: null`, or a `null` one beside a spec path, THEN the system SHALL refuse the document.

requirements.title: The planning skill teaches the key
requirements.statement: The bundled phax-planning skill shall define `completes-spec` in its plan frontmatter section: its two values, its absence on a spec-less plan, and the rule that every plan of a spec except the last says `false`.

nonGoals: No change to the chain gate's rule. It still applies on top of `completes-spec: true`.
No change to completing a spec by hand (`phax artifact complete`) or to plan completion.
No cross-plan lint advisories: `plans lint` does not warn about two live plans that both say `true` for one spec, or about a spec whose live plans all say `false` (see §9).
No inference of the last plan from anything phax can see: plan counts, slugs, order, or the spec's text.

No migration of archived plans. Archived plans with a source spec predate the key and are not revalidated by any run or chain-gate flow. An artifact command pointed directly at one refuses it, as the no-shims rule accepts for any persisted-format change.
No `completes-spec` in `phax-plan.json`: the extracted plan stays lineage-free.
Out of scope: approval-ground, the per-file approval records (shipped in 0.19.0), and batching several plans per run (spec 24).

acceptanceCriteria.name: A plan that states its intent validates
acceptanceCriteria.given: a live made-up plan whose `source-spec` names an existing spec and whose frontmatter carries `completes-spec: true` (and, separately, `completes-spec: false`)
acceptanceCriteria.then: no artifact-validation refusal occurs and the value is read as given

acceptanceCriteria.name: A plan with a source spec but no completes-spec is refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: a live plan whose `source-spec` names a spec and whose frontmatter has no `completes-spec`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax plans lint <plan>` runs, and separately `phax artifact approve <plan>`
acceptanceCriteria.then: each exits 12 naming `completes-spec`, and approve writes nothing

acceptanceCriteria.name: A non-boolean value is refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: a live plan with a source spec and `completes-spec: "yes"`

acceptanceCriteria.name: A spec-less plan must not carry the key
acceptanceCriteria.given: a live plan with `source-spec: null` and `completes-spec: false`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits 12 naming `completes-spec`; the same plan without the key validates

acceptanceCriteria.name: The completing plan completes its spec
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Approved spec whose only live plan is Approved with `completes-spec: true`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the plan's run turns its final phase green
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run branch carries the plan's and the spec's completion commits, the spec lives under docs/specs/archive/, and the output lists both completions as today

acceptanceCriteria.name: A completing plan still respects the chain gate
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Approved spec named by two Approved live plans, the running one with `completes-spec: true`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the spec's status and location are unchanged on the run branch and the output reports the skip naming the other plan, as today

acceptanceCriteria.name: A non-completing plan leaves its spec live
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Approved spec whose only live plan is Approved with `completes-spec: false`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the plan's run turns its final phase green
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run branch carries the plan's completion commit only; the spec reads Approved under docs/specs/, its approval record file under docs/specs/approvals/ still exists, and the output contains a `kept` line saying the plan does not complete it

acceptanceCriteria.name: The handoff and PR body name the spec outcome
acceptanceCriteria.given: three runs whose plans name a source spec, ending completed, kept because blocked, and kept because `completes-spec: false`
acceptanceCriteria.when: each run opens review and `phax publish-pr` builds the PR body
acceptanceCriteria.then: each review-handoff.md and PR body state that run's spec outcome with the spec path; a run of a spec-less plan states none

acceptanceCriteria.name: Flipping the value makes the plan stale
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Approved plan with `completes-spec: false` that `phax plans status` reports fresh
acceptanceCriteria.when: the value is edited to `true` and `phax plans status` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the plan is reported stale with reason `self-changed`

acceptanceCriteria.name: Plan creation writes the stated value
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax artifact new plan widgets --spec docs/specs/2609291000-widgets.md --not-last` runs (and separately with `--last`)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the created plan's frontmatter reads `completes-spec: false` (respectively `true`) after `source-spec`, and the confirmation line names the value

acceptanceCriteria.name: Plan creation refuses an unstated or meaningless value
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax artifact new plan widgets --spec <spec>` runs with neither flag, then with both, then `phax artifact new plan catalog-refresh --last` runs without `--spec`
acceptanceCriteria.then: each exits 12 and no plan file is written

acceptanceCriteria.name: Headless authoring takes the value from the flags
acceptanceCriteria.given: `phax artifact new plan widgets --spec <spec> --not-last --headless --brief brief.md` against a stubbed session that returns `completesSpec: true`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the committed sidecar carries `completesSpec: false` and the rendered plan's frontmatter reads `completes-spec: false`

acceptanceCriteria.name: The plan document enforces the variant
acceptanceCriteria.given: `phax artifact schema plan` and stubbed session documents
acceptanceCriteria.when: a document omits `completesSpec`, or pairs `sourceSpec: null` with `completesSpec: true`, or a spec path with `completesSpec: null`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the printed schema lists `completesSpec` as required, and each such document is refused with nothing written

acceptanceCriteria.name: The planning skill teaches the key
acceptanceCriteria.when: its plan frontmatter section is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: it defines `completes-spec` with values `true` and `false`, says it is absent when `source-spec` is `null`, and says every plan of a spec except the last carries `false`

openQuestions.question: How does a run know its plan is the last of its spec? Decided by the author on 2026-10-05; not reopened.

options.label: A required plan field (`completes-spec: true|false`); the run completes the spec only when it is true, with the chain gate on top
options.abandons: zero-touch plan authoring: every plan with a spec must now state one more fact, and the format changes before the 1.0 freeze

options.label: Never complete a spec at run end; leave it to `phax artifact complete`
options.abandons: the spec's completion landing in the same merge as the last plan's work, which spec 27 put there on purpose

options.label: Infer the last plan from what phax can see
options.abandons: correctness: nothing persisted says how many plans a spec will have, so any inference repeats the defect

openQuestions.rationale: Decided 2026-10-05. Only the author knows whether more plans follow, so the plan must say it. A required field keeps spec 27's single merge for the last plan and costs one stated fact per plan.

openQuestions.question: Where does the value live, and how do the frontmatter, the plan document and phax-plan.json stay consistent? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: Frontmatter key `completes-spec` is the value phax reads; the plan document mirrors it as `completesSpec`, set from the CLI like `sourceSpec`; phax-plan.json does not carry it
options.abandons: a single copy: a hand edit of the frontmatter after authoring leaves the sidecar's mirror behind, exactly as `sourceSpec` can drift today

options.label: Frontmatter only; the plan document is unchanged
options.abandons: the sidecar as the full authored lineage: its readers (schemas-package consumers, the cockpit) see `sourceSpec` but cannot tell whether the plan completes it

options.label: A field of phax-plan.json
options.abandons: a deterministic read: the extracted plan is derived, cached and model-assisted, and holds phases rather than lineage, so the run's decision would rest on an extraction

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended. Lineage already lives in the frontmatter beside `source-spec`. The approval fingerprint covers it there, and run completion already reads that block. The mirror follows the established `sourceSpec` precedent, so the sidecar stays a complete description. Its drift risk is the same one `sourceSpec` has, and phax never reads the mirror to decide anything.

openQuestions.question: What does a plan with `source-spec: null` carry? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: No `completes-spec` key; its presence is refused (the plan document carries `completesSpec: null`, since every document key is required)
options.abandons: a uniform key set: the allowed frontmatter keys now depend on the `source-spec` variant, and the frontmatter and document spell "not applicable" differently (absent vs null)

options.label: `completes-spec: false` required
options.abandons: meaning: `false` claims a decision about a spec that does not exist, and `true` beside `null` becomes a nonsense value that lint must police

options.label: `completes-spec: null` required
options.abandons: economy: a key with no information that every spec-less plan, loose plan.md included, must still write

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended. Explicit per-variant shapes beat a permissive superset. The key exists exactly where it means something, and each variant has one legal form. The document uses null only because its own rule forbids missing keys.

openQuestions.question: How does `phax artifact new plan` set the value? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: With `--spec`, exactly one of `--last` / `--not-last` is required and authoritative in both interactive and headless modes; either flag without `--spec` is refused
options.abandons: a zero-decision `artifact new plan` for the common one-plan spec, plus every existing invocation and example gaining a flag

options.label: Default `true` with `--spec`; `--not-last` opts out
options.abandons: protection where the defect arose: the author of plan 1/5 who forgets the flag gets today's behavior, caught only if someone reads the frontmatter at approval

options.label: In headless mode the session decides from the brief
options.abandons: determinism: an agent guesses a lineage fact, and interactive creation still needs another rule

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended, with shorter flag names: `--last` / `--not-last` (the frontmatter key stays `completes-spec`). The defect is a silent default. Forcing the statement at creation costs one flag, while a default reproduces the defect for anyone who does not think about it. Making the flags authoritative in headless mode mirrors how `--spec` governs `sourceSpec`.

openQuestions.question: Does `plans lint` warn about two live plans both saying `true` for one spec, or a spec whose live plans all say `false`? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: Neither; lint checks the plan it is given, as today
options.abandons: an early hint that a multi-plan spec's statements look odd

options.label: Advisory warnings for both cases
options.abandons: signal honesty: all-`false` is the designed state while the last plan is unwritten (plans authored one at a time), and two `true` plans are handled harmlessly by the chain gate, so both warnings fire on legitimate paths and train warning-blindness

options.label: Warn only on two live `true` plans
options.abandons: lint's single-plan scope: it must scan sibling plans for a case the chain gate already makes harmless

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended. Neither situation is a defect. The chain gate already makes two `true` plans safe, and the run output and handoff show each non-completing plan's choice. Spec 27 rejected a warning on a designed path for the same reason.

openQuestions.question: How do live plans gain the field? (Decided by the author on 2026-10-06; not reopened.)

options.label: By hand, in the implementing plan
options.abandons: a repeatable path for other repositories with live plans that name a spec

options.label: A one-time migration command
options.abandons: scope: a new command, and the decision it cannot make (whether each plan is its spec's last) still falls to a human

openQuestions.rationale: Decided by the author on 2026-10-06, as recommended. Nobody else runs multi-plan specs, and the value is a judgement no command can supply. The only live plan here today has `source-spec: null` and needs nothing under q-specless. Any plan with a spec that goes live before the implementing run lands gains the key by hand. If it is Approved, it is re-approved, since the key is fingerprinted.

settled: The value lives in the plan frontmatter as `completes-spec` (`true` | `false`). It is present exactly when `source-spec` names a spec and refused beside `source-spec: null`. This applies to every plan the frontmatter decoder reads, loose plan.md included.

Run completion reads `completes-spec` from the pre-transition plan Markdown, as it reads `source-spec` today. `true` keeps today's ride-along unchanged. `false` makes no spec transition and reports the spec as kept.
The run completion report distinguishes the two kept reasons as named variants: blocked by live plans (with the blocking plans), and not completed by this plan.

`completes-spec` is fingerprinted: `fingerprintSource` keeps dropping only `status` and `approved`. Changing it on an Approved plan makes it `self-changed`. This is intended, because the value changes what the run does to the repository and so is part of what was approved.

The plan document gains a required `completesSpec` (boolean beside a spec path, null beside `sourceSpec: null`). phax sets it from the CLI flags whatever the session returned, and the authoring prompt states the value as it states `sourceSpec`.
`plans lint` refuses through artifact validation (exit 12), not through a finding. No cross-plan advisories.
Live plans are migrated by hand. Today no live plan here needs a change.
open: Exact flag spelling for `phax artifact new plan` (the required opposite pair is settled), and the wording of the refusal, kept and handoff lines.

How the plan-document shape change is recorded in the schemas package's format history (release stamp, the step for sidecars written before the key). Follow the package's procedure; no live sidecar exists in this repository.
Where in review-handoff.md the spec outcome sits.
constraints: No change to the chain gate's rule, to `phax artifact complete`, or to plan completion.
No back-compat: the key is required where it applies; no default is inferred for a plan that lacks it.
Tests use made-up plans and specs, never this repository's own.

This changes the plan format and the `artifact new plan` CLI contract, so it lands before the 1.0 freeze (NEXT_STEPS §Road to 1.0.0). Update phax.usage.kdl and the completion/spec-lint gates that read it.

Docs: the phax-planning skill's §Plan frontmatter block; the README lifecycle sentence "A run completes its own plan, and its spec where it can"; the `artifact new plan` long help (skeleton keys and the flags); close the NEXT_STEPS follow-up and drop the artifact-decide note about reverting the run's spec completion by hand.
